```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
V <- load_va()
APP <- "https://adamdennett-school-information-system.share.connect.posit.cloud/"
# The simulator's schools, from the app's own data (R/40_app_data.R): each school's
# latest model year, its inputs and its results
S <- readRDS(here::here("app", "data", "app_data.rds"))$sim$schools
b <- function(g, t) V$coefs$estimate[V$coefs$group == g & V$coefs$term == t]
ab_pct <- function(g, rel) 100 * ((1 + rel)^b(g, "log(PERCTOT)") - 1)
```

The School Information System replaces this page's earlier in-browser
simulator. It sets Attainment 8 beside Value Added v2.1 for all,
disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged pupils (with girls and boys), over
four years, a single year or a moving average, for every state secondary
school in England. Its tabs:

- **School Finder:** a school by area, name or map, with its results,
  value added and absence against expected, year by year.
- **Find My Twin:** the schools most like it in intake and setting, and the
  look-alikes that do better.
- **Observed vs Predicted:** every school's Attainment 8 and absence against
  what its intake predicts.
- **Policy Simulator:** what the model expects if a school's, or a whole
  area's, absence or intake were different (how it works is below).
- **Area Overview:** a region, combined or mayoral authority, local
  authority, district or academy trust.
- **Travel and Distance:** distance and journey times to school, and the
  national walking routes as they are completed.

The app runs on Posit Connect Cloud and may take a few seconds to wake up.
Its code is in [`app/`](https://github.com/adamdennett/school_value_added/tree/main/app)
and its data are built by `R/40_app_data.R` from the files behind this site.

## How the simulator works {#sec-how}

The simulator uses the fitted [Value Added v2.1](method.qmd) models, one for
each group of pupils. Each model explains the log of a school's Attainment 8
by its intake and setting, so every lever changes a school's expected
result by a *percentage*:

$$\text{Attainment 8}_\text{new} = \text{Attainment 8}_\text{latest} \times
\exp\Big(\sum_j \beta_j \, \Delta x_j\Big)$$

where $\Delta x_j$ is the change in each lever (in logs for absence,
disadvantage and EAL, which enter the model as logs) and $\beta_j$ is its
coefficient for that group. Everything else about the school stays as it
was, including what the model cannot explain: its value added. A school
starts from its latest published result (`r yl(max(S$sim_year))` for
most), not from its prediction.

For all pupils, cutting a school's absence by a tenth (say from 9% to
8.1%) goes with Attainment 8 `r pts(ab_pct("all", -0.1), 1)`% higher, about
`r pts(ab_pct("all", -0.1) * mean(S$a_all) / 100, 1)` points at the average
school. For disadvantaged pupils it is `r pts(ab_pct("disadvantaged", -0.1), 1)`%, and for
non-disadvantaged pupils `r pts(ab_pct("non_disadvantaged", -0.1), 1)`%.
**The same cut in absence helps disadvantaged pupils more**, so it narrows
the gap.

In area mode, every school in the area gets the same change, and the area's
result is the average of its schools' results weighted by their number of
pupils.

### What it can and cannot tell you

- **It is the model's arithmetic, not a forecast.** The coefficients
  describe how results differ between schools with different absence and
  intake, all else equal. They are not experiments. A school that cut its
  absence would not necessarily gain exactly this, and how it cut it would
  matter.
- **Absence is not a dial.** The absence lever says what better attendance
  would be worth, not how to get it. See [How school absence
  changes](absence_change.qmd) for what moves it.
- **The intake levers are not policies.** They show how much of a school's
  result is its pupils. Moving them is a way of seeing that, or of thinking
  through an admissions change, not something a school can do.
- **The groups are modelled separately.** Each group has its own
  coefficients, so the same change can do more for one group than another.
  The all-pupils result is its own model, not an average of the others.

### What changed from the original

The [original School Attainment Policy Simulator](https://adam-dennett.shinyapps.io/School_Attainment_Policy_Simulator/)
(v1.0) ran on the first model. This version follows [the review's](review.qmd)
recommendations:

- **No Ofsted grade or workforce levers.** They are no longer in the
  expectation.
- **New levers:** SEN support, EHC plans, pupil mobility and neighbourhood
  education.
- **Value added beside Attainment 8**, for girls and boys as well as
  disadvantaged and other pupils, over four years or year by year.
- **Area mode:** the same change across every school in a district,
  authority, combined authority, region, trust or England.
- **Absence against expected** and **travel and distance** are new.
